title: Tenant-impact simulator and adaptive admission playbook for hosted GPU pools
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Summary: Following the 2026-01-29 hosted API capacity exhaustion event we observed a prolonged queue buildup and tenant-level unfairness that amplified tail latency. Root cause analysis showed a combination of a traffic spike from a new customer feature, a regression in admission scoring that disabled early fast-fail for long-running prefetch requests, and insufficient synthetic coverage to catch the regression prior to deploy. This ticket is dedicated to building a tenant-aware simulation harness, formalizing adaptive admission thresholds, and automating a preemptive rescale/priming workflow so similar capacity exhaustion events are detected and mitigated before customer impact grows. The goal is twofold: (1) create a reproducible synthetic load runner and tenant-impact scoring model that can exercise admission logic at scale, and (2) produce an actionable playbook and automation to adapt thresholds and trigger prewarm/rescale flows when high risk is detected.
action_items: Build a tenant-impact simulator that can replay multi-tenant traffic mixes, KV/cache hit patterns, and prefetch behavior (owner: Marco Chen, ETA: 2026-03-04).
Add regression tests that run the simulator in CI against admission-scoring code paths (owner: SRE team, ETA: 2026-03-11).
Implement adaptive admission thresholds with exponential backoff + tenant scoring; enable a soft-fail mode toggle for progressive rollout (owner: Runtime team, ETA: 2026-03-18).

Create automated preemptive priming workflow: when simulator or metric-based detectors signal risk, trigger a reserved-capacity prewarm and/or reduce prefetch aggressiveness (owner: Autoscale team, ETA: 2026-03-25).
Ship a Grafana dashboard with tenant-level risk heatmap and a Slack alerting runbook link (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-03-10).
Run a canary of adaptive admission logic against 5% of traffic for 72h and validate no accuracy regressions for top customers (owner: QA + Product, ETA: 2026-04-01).
